concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: On 15 September 2026, the original DPA provision was in force and required notification without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after the Processor became aware of a breach.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment replacing the original deadline took effect on 1 October 2026, requiring notification without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after awareness.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduced the prior written notice period for routine on-site audits from 30 days to 20 days. The annex's shorter notice period does not override the amendment's main body.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment in force on 1 November 2026 sets the Processor's aggregate liability cap at EUR 1,000,000, replacing the earlier fee-based alternative.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality obligations.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor in the DPA, and its approval was not withdrawn until 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The amendment expressly withdraws Meridian Mail Ltd's approval with effect from 1 January 2027, so it is not approved on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, the distinct authorised processing countries are Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France, and Denmark.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: The amended return-and-deletion period is 60 days, so termination on 31 December 2026 results in a latest deletion or return date of 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. the notice must include the required breach details, and the processor must document the breach and cooperate with the controller on any required regulatory or data-subject communications.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The notice must include the required breach details, and the Processor must document the breach and cooperate with the Controller on any required regulatory or data-subject communications.
justifications: The amended breach clause sets a 24-hour outer limit while retaining the separate duty to act without undue delay, and the surrounding provisions specify the notice contents, documentation, and cooperation duties.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The expedited regime applies because the breach exposed usable privileged credentials, triggering a 12-hour outer limit from original awareness.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Original awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April, making the 12-hour deadline 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice arrived at 06:00, which was 50 minutes late.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The follow-up report is due by the end of the third Business Day after awareness. After excluding the 12 April closure and the approved pause on 14 April, the third counted Business Day is 16 April 2027.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 60 calendar days after termination on 30 June 2027. The later applicable deadline is the tenth Business Day after the final hold ends on 25 August, which falls on 9 September 2027 because 30 August is excluded.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deadline and 35 calendar days after creation. Thirty-five calendar days after its creation on 30 June 2027 is 4 August 2027, earlier than the ordinary deletion deadline.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: On 1 September 2027, the records remain within the post-release deletion window and may be used only for legal preservation. Service delivery and analytics are expressly prohibited, and the analytics retention request was rejected.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval could begin only after the proposed start date, written consent, and completed security review. The security review completed on 22 April, later than the other conditions, and processing began that day.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: This entity was approved from 1 January 2027 and continued ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd was withdrawn and its later emergency permission expressly excluded ordinary customer transactional email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: On 15 May 2027, processing and effective authorisation are established for existing storage in Norway, Tallinn operations in Estonia, ordinary email in France, monitoring in Lithuania, and Stockholm infrastructure in Sweden. Denmark had been withdrawn, Finland had not begun processing or obtained consent, Germany lacked required approval, and Ireland's incident-only permission had expired.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT and deducting the qualifying service credit, so twice the fees is EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 floor. This is the security cap before the earlier security payment.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 and EUR 300,000 has already been paid for ordinary breaches in the current Contract Year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary loss is payable up to the remaining EUR 700,000, the single shared security loss is payable at EUR 1,750,000 within the remaining security pool, and the two confidentiality losses total EUR 350,000 and remain uncapped. The overlapping security claims for the same loss are counted once.
